page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, which yields a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled, consisting of a 2458 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU evaluations, and Geekbench multi-core suites, including software compilation and ray tracing. Large-block memory read and write bandwidth are also highly rated, reaching 291.37 GB/sec and 132.39 GB/sec respectively. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores.

This hardware profile is highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving, supported by a Redis SET performance of 62.19 million operations per second. It is also capable of handling prompt processing for small and medium language models. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU results in weak performance for large-scale LLM text generation, with the 70B model text generation benchmark falling into the bottom 25%. It is best suited for enterprise databases, CI/CD pipelines, and high-traffic web applications.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DDSv5 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) running at 2.8 GHz, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 2458 GB local SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers strong multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, making it highly capable for parallel processing tasks. While single-core benchmarks and large-scale LLM text generation are average to weak due to the lack of GPU acceleration, the system excels in database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving. The balanced resource density of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU offers a solid qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for enterprise-scale workloads requiring fast local storage and high multi-threaded compute capacity.
